channel.title: Waseeq Ur Rehman
channel.description: Recent content on Waseeq Ur Rehman

item.title: ACRS - Automated Cyber Reasoning System
item.description: Final Year Project — an automated vulnerability discovery, analysis, and remediation framework combining static analysis, symbolic execution, fuzzing, and LLM reasoning into a single research-oriented pipeline.

item.title: Automated DevSecOps Pipeline for Android Applications
item.description: A fully automated Android security pipeline built on Jenkins across two AWS EC2 instances, integrating Semgrep, Gitleaks, SonarQube, Trivy, MobSF, and DefectDojo to cover every security layer from source to APK.

item.title: I Built a Security Pipeline That Scans Every Android Build Automatically
item.description: A walkthrough of why I built an automated Android DevSecOps pipeline and what it covers - from SAST to APK-level mobile analysis, all wired into a single vulnerability dashboard.

item.title: Client-Side Access Control is Not Access Control: Firestore Query Tampering via Frida
item.description: Bypassing Frida detection in Notely AI and tampering with Firestore queries at runtime via ObjC method hooking to access archived admin notes.

item.title: Chaining Deep Link Injection with SQLi to Leak Sensitive Data from an iOS App
item.description: Chaining deep link URL scheme handling with SQL injection in an iOS crypto wallet app to extract another user's recovery key via a UNION-based query.

item.title: Defeating Multi-Layer Anti-Reversing Protections on iOS with Static Analysis and Frida
item.description: Bypassing a multi-layered RASP/compliance check system in Captain NoHook using static analysis with r2/nm to locate functions, Frida to replace them, and Objection to find the hidden flag in memory.

item.title: One Hook to Bypass All: Defeating iOS Jailbreak Detection with Frida
item.description: Bypassing iOS jailbreak detection in No Escape by hooking the root isJailbroken() export with Frida, then using Objection to find the flag in memory.

item.title: Exploiting SQLite Injection via Username Field Concatenation on Android
item.description: Exploiting SQL injection in an Android app's signup function via username field concatenation to register a Pro account with 10,000 credits.

item.title: Two Ways to Break a Hardcoded PIN: AES Bruteforce vs Frida Hooking
item.description: Two approaches to bypass a PIN check in an IoT Android app: offline AES bruteforce to recover the key (345), and runtime Frida hook to skip the check entirely.

item.title: Unsafe YAML Deserialization to RCE on Android
item.description: Exploiting an unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization flow chained with a legacy command execution utility to achieve RCE on an Android app.

item.title: Overflowing a JNI Buffer to Hijack system() in an Android Native Library
item.description: Exploiting a native stack buffer overflow in Note Keeper's JNI code to overwrite a command buffer adjacent to the overflow target, achieving arbitrary command execution via system().

item.title: About
item.description:
I’m Waseeq Ur Rehman, based in Islamabad, Pakistan. I spend most of my time breaking things and occasionally writing about it. Outside of security, I’m a football enthusiast (Blaugrana blood) and a gamer. In CTFs I compete as Gus Fring, mostly with teams PsychoTherapist and Akatsuki.

What I Do

My work covers Mobile Application Security (Android & iOS), Web Application Security, API Security Testing, and Network Security. On the more technical end I do Reverse Engineering, Binary Analysis and Exploit Development. I also did some work in the DevSecOps space, building security into pipelines rather than bolting it on after the fact.
